endorsements.quote: One approach is to encourage clinicians to document the use of generative AI in their notes.

As healthcare systems adopt language models in higher-order reasoning tasks such as diagnostics, providing uncertainty metrics along the model output to the end users will allow clinicians to better assess model performance and help minimize the risk of potential harms to the patients.

Providing the reference to the source knowledge could also help in applications such as ambient documentation where the model can link its output to the verbatim transcription of patient-clinician conversation.

In addition, diagnostic decision-support requires rigorous evaluation across the full spectrum of disease phenotypes in interactive AI-human settings, as these models might be prone to making more errors in detecting certain pathologies than humans26.

unlisted_practices: Tag AI-generated content by default at the vendor level, similar to how copied content in the EHR is flagged.
Use watermarking or other embedded tagging at the point of generation to trace LLM-generated content, treating it as an imperfect tool within a broader traceability framework.
Account for clinician reviews and modifications of AI-generated content when enforcing traceability of hybrid human-AI documentation.
Customize evaluation benchmarks to the specific objectives of each generative AI application.
Maintain clear distinctions between human and AI contributions in the EHR to ensure accountability and continuous quality improvement.
Preserve human-generated data for training future language models by distinguishing human-written from AI-produced notes.
